name: Streams
tagline: A Kafka broker and a Confluent Schema Registry that decode every Avro message and break on cue.

capabilities.title: The real Kafka protocol
capabilities.text: Produce, Fetch, ListOffsets, Metadata, CreateTopics and consumer groups with JoinGroup, SyncGroup, Heartbeat and offset commits.

capabilities.title: Avro, decoded
capabilities.text: Values in Confluent framing are decoded with their registry schema, so you read JSON, not bytes. JSON and text values too.

capabilities.title: A Schema Registry
capabilities.text: Confluent-compatible subjects and versions; register Avro, JSON or Protobuf schemas. The same schema keeps its id.

capabilities.title: Produce as the partner
capabilities.text: produce sends a key, value, headers and partition; with a subject the value is Avro-encoded with that schema.

capabilities.title: Consumer groups and lag
capabilities.text: Members, assigned partitions and the lag of each partition: committed offset against the high watermark.

capabilities.title: Force a rebalance
capabilities.text: rebalance makes members get REBALANCE_IN_PROGRESS on their next heartbeat, so they must join again.

capabilities.title: SASL logins
capabilities.text: PLAIN and SCRAM-SHA-256/512. With sasl_required and no users listed, any user works and any password except wrong.

capabilities.title: Broker-level failures
capabilities.text: Leader not available, SASL refused, slow fetch, duplicated records and a Schema Registry that answers 503.

callouts.title: Topics
callouts.text: Each topic with its partitions and message count; made when a client asks, unless auto_create is off.

callouts.title: How to connect
callouts.text: Kafka on localhost:9092 and the Schema Registry on :8081.

callouts.title: Partition and offset
callouts.text: Where each record landed, to check keys go to the partition the app expects.

callouts.title: Avro, readable
callouts.text: The value decoded with schema 3 from the registry, not raw bytes.

callouts.title: Key
callouts.text: The record key, which picks the partition as a real producer would.

callouts.title: Registry subject
callouts.text: With a subject, the value is Avro-encoded with that schema in Confluent framing.

callouts.title: Produce
callouts.text: Sends the record as the partner would; the app's consumer reads it on its next fetch.

callouts.title: Leader not available
callouts.text: Producers and consumers get LEADER_NOT_AVAILABLE until you set Normal.

callouts.title: Registry down
callouts.text: The Schema Registry answers 503: does the app retry or drop the record?

provoke.name: Duplicated records
provoke.what: Each record is kept twice: is the consumer idempotent?

provoke.name: Rebalance
provoke.what: Members get REBALANCE_IN_PROGRESS and must rejoin

provoke.name: Unknown schema id
provoke.what: A record the consumer cannot decode

provoke.name: No such topic
provoke.what: Topics are not created on demand

advantages.title: One process, not a cluster
advantages.text: No ZooKeeper, KRaft or registry containers. Kafka and the Schema Registry start with Stuntman in seconds.

advantages.title: Messages you can read
advantages.text: Avro values are shown decoded with their schema, so a test checks fields, not bytes.

advantages.title: Failures a cluster hides
advantages.text: Duplicates, rebalances and a missing leader happen on request, so consumer code is tested where it breaks.

advantages.title: Act as the partner
advantages.text: Produce the partner's records with the right schema, or a bad one, without access to their cluster.

agent.prompt: Send a shipment event twice and check the app's consumer does not create a duplicate.
steps: shipments-worker · lag 0 on 3 partitions · 2 records read
tools: Topics with partitions, messages, high watermarks

notes: One broker node; batches uncompressed or gzip (snappy, lz4, zstd refused); compatibility checks always answer compatible.
One port serves every environment: the default one answers.
